label: Seafloor habitats
blurb: Seafloor features linked to uniqueness and fragility: seamounts and guyots, ridges, trenches and the hadal zone, and active hydrothermal vents.

headlines.label: Provisional seafloor habitats score
headlines.note: The score is the mean of this pillar's variable percentiles among EBSAs, from 0 to 100.

charts.title: Percentile by variable

method: Feature shares are the area of the EBSA's res-6 cells that carry the named feature types in the global seafloor geomorphology map (Harris et al. 2014), divided by the EBSA's area. Feature layers overlap, so each cell is counted once. Active vents are InterRidge v3.4 vent fields marked active (confirmed or inferred). Most EBSAs have no vent and no trench; those ties share the midpoint of their rank range. These features stand for uniqueness, rarity and fragility (BBNJ Annex I criteria a, b and g) only loosely. Scores are mid-rank percentiles (0–100) among the EBSAs with data, with direction applied so higher is better for the pillar; tied values share the midpoint of their rank range. The pillar score is the plain mean of the variable percentiles. All of this is provisional.
